title: Prominent immigrant rights group endorses Ferguson’s reelection bid
summary: Less than a week after Gov. Wes Moore released a list of Democratic endorsements that snubbed Senate President Bill Ferguson, the political arm of a prominent immigrant rights and advocacy group this week endorsed Ferguson as "the right leader moving forward."
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters May 15, 2026

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters May 15, 2026

Less than a week after Gov. Wes Moore (D) released a list of Democratic endorsements that snubbed Senate President Bill Ferguson (D-Baltimore City), the political arm of the prominent immigrant rights and advocacy group this week endorsed Ferguson as “the right leader moving forward.”

It was one of 143 endorsements released Wednesday by CASA in Action for Maryland congressional, state and county races. It is the political arm of We Are CASA, the immigrant rights organization that heavily involved in passage of bills in this year’s legislative session that expanded protections against immigration detention and deportation.

The list included several Democrats who were not endorsed by Moore, but Ferguson was the most noteworthy.

“Our board looked at the totality of his [Ferguson’s] tenure in the Senate, we concluded he is the right leader moving forward,” Cathryn Jackson, policy director for CASA in Action, said Thursday.

“Since he became Senate president, Maryland has passed legislation that has made a real difference in people’s lives,” Jackson said. “This year we were able to get the Data Privacy Act, Community Trust Act [and] 287(g) passed. These are all victories that ultimately Bill Ferguson got on board with and delivered.”

While it was a shot in the arm for Ferguson, it was a setback for Bobby LaPin, the social media personality and charter boat captain who is challenging Ferguson in the June 23 Democratic primary for the District 46 Senate seat. LaPin has built much of his campaign around Ferguson’s opposition to congressional redistricting and what LaPin says have been failures on immigration legislation.

Moore issues scores of endorsements, but some incumbent Democrats miss the cut

LaPin released a statement via text message Thursday about the CASA endorsement.

“Bill Ferguson let the Community Trust Act sit for five years and only moved it in an election year. That’s not leadership, that’s politics,” the statement said. “The people I’ve marched with and immigrant families we’ve stood beside against ICE know that.

“I respect the work CASA does for immigrant families, and look forward to continue working with them in the Senate. But this endorsement says more about how power works in Annapolis than it does about what’s best for the communities they serve,” he said.

Ferguson thanked CASA for the endorsement with a message on social media about the work ahead responding to President Donald Trump (R) and his administration.

“At a moment when the Trump Administration is targeting, threatening, and terrorizing immigrant families throughout Baltimore — including around our schools — it’s up to each of us to do our part,” Ferguson said.

Immigration activists had a relatively good year in the legislature this year, after seeing a last-minute defeat in 2025 of one of their priorities, a bill to ban 287(g) agreements between local police agencies and federal immigration officials.

The General Assembly was in session for barely a month this year before those bills, Senate Bill 245 and House Bill 444, had been passed as emergency measures and signed into law by the governor, taking effect immediately with his signature on Feb. 17.

Lawmakers also approved bills to further limit the ability of Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers to operate within the state, complementing the 287(g) ban. Senate Bill 791 – the Community Trust Act – was approved on the session’s last day. Supporters say it will complement the 287(g) bills by making it harder to sheriffs’ departments to skirt the ban.

Another immigration-related measure to win final-day approval was the Data Privacy Act,which seeks to close loopholes in the state’s Public Information Act and prohibit a business from selling personal data of an individual “for the purpose of immigration enforcement.”

There were far more similarities than differences between the CASA in Action list and the governor’s. But among the candidates endorsed by CASA in Action who did not make the governor’s list are:

“With these candidates, it’s important to know that we spend a great deal of time reflecting on the needs at this moment and the progress we have made in the last several years. It isn’t easy to come to a decision,” Jackson said. “No matter who gets elected, we will be there fighting and holding them accountable.”

— This story was updated at 2 p.m. Friday to correct the spelling of Cathryn Jackson’s first name.
